newsitem.title: UK: Church accused of double standards over gays.
newsitem.headline: Church accused of double standards over gays.

text.p: Gay campaigners on Sunday accused the Church of England of hypocrisy, claiming almost half its bishops were secretly ignoring a rule forbidding the ordination as priests of active homosexuals.
The Lesbian and Gay Christian Movement said a survey it had carried out showed that 19 of the 44 diocesan bishops had ordained people they had known to be in same-sex relationships.

"It is obvious the church now has no option but to drop the damaging and dishonest pretence that it is not ordaining practising homosexuals in considerable numbers," the movement's general secretary, Richard Kirker, said in a statement.
The movement announced details of the survey on the eve of a debate in the church's governing General Synod in the northern city of York on a document setting out the Church's views on sex.
Synod members who oppose gay priests have put down an amendment which would reaffirm that "God's calling to all people requires chastity outside of marriage and fidelity within it".

Kirker said his group had surveyed 1,200 priests. The results had also shown that 37 of the 44 bishops had employed at least one already-ordained priest whom they knew to have partners of the same sex.

Monday's debate, hailed by Kirker as the first time in 10 years that the synod has discussed gay and lesbian issues, could lead to fresh dtensions in the Church of England over the way it chooses priests.
The Church, the established religion in England with Queen Elizabeth as the "defender of the faith", has been riven in recent years by a decision to allow women to join the ranks of its clergy.
This has led to the resignation of several priests, with some high-profile defections to Catholicism.
But Kirker said the survey meant the Church had no alternative but to resolve the issue of homosexual ordination. "The double standard must end," he said.
The Anglican Church has 80 million members worldwide.
